understand.concept: An inventory manager tracks product identifiers, names, quantities and prices. It validates stock changes, searches records and persists data. It should prevent negative quantities and define behaviour for duplicate identifiers.
understand.whyItMatters: The project combines data modeling, array or dynamic collection management, file I/O and business-rule validation.

explain.narrative:
An inventory manager tracks product identifiers, names, quantities and prices. It validates stock changes, searches records and persists data. It should prevent negative quantities and define behaviour for duplicate identifiers.

For a complete implementation, define input constraints, ownership, error handling and test cases before coding. Compile with warnings and verify normal, boundary and failure behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The structure groups the inventory fields. Validation rejects negative quantity or price in this simplified model; a complete application must also validate input and persistence errors.

practise.guidedTask: Define the invariants for quantity, price and product ID.
practise.independentTask: Implement add stock, reduce stock, lookup and save/load. Test insufficient stock and duplicate IDs.
hints: Separate business rules from terminal input and file output.
Use an integer minor currency unit if exact decimal accounting is required.
Check every file operation and validate loaded records.
